十一月三号，美国人去投票。选票上没有特朗普的名字，可这次投票，决定了他接下来两年: On November third, Americans went to the polls. Trump's name wasn't on the ballot. But this vote decided how much he can still get done in the next two years.

中期选举到底选什么？特朗普接下来会被怎样卡住？和你的股票账户又有什么关系？一个一: What do the midterms actually decide? How will Trump be boxed in? And what does it mean for your brokerage account? Let's take them one at a time.
一张选票，改写整个国会: One ballot rewrites all of Congress
先花三十秒，把规则讲清楚。: First, thirty seconds on the rules.
总统一届四年。特朗普这一届，从二零二五年一月开始。: A president serves four years. Trump's term started in January twenty twenty-five.
走到第二年年底，正好是任期的一半，所以叫中期选举。: The end of the second year is exactly halfway through the term, so they're called the midterms.
总统本人要等到二零二八年。这一次，换的是国会和各州的人。: The president himself isn't up until twenty twenty-eight. This time, it's Congress and the states that change hands.
拿到选票，第一项是众议员。全国四百三十五个席位，同一天全部重选。: First on the ballot is the House. All four hundred thirty-five seats nationwide are up on the same day.
第二项是参议员。参议员一当六年，这次只换三十五席，大约三分之一。: Second is the Senate. Senators serve six years, and only thirty-five seats are up this time, about a third.
第三项是州长，三十六个州同时换人。: Third is governor. Thirty-six states pick new governors at the same time.
参议院改选约三分之一: About a third of the Senate up
一句话：中期选举，就是选民给总统的期中考。: In short: the midterms are the voters' midterm exam for the president.
两院一起翻蓝，七个州翻转: Both chambers flip blue, seven states flip
那这次的结果，到底有多夸张？: So just how dramatic were the results?
先看选前。众议院和参议院，红色都过了中线，也就是都在共和党手里。: First, before the election. In both the House and the Senate, red was past the center line, meaning Republicans controlled both.
开票后，众议院的蓝色一路越过中线。民主党已经拿到两百五十四席，还有十九席没出结果: As the votes came in, blue in the House surged past the center line. Democrats have two hundred fifty-four seats, with nineteen still uncalled.
参议院也丢了：民主党党团 54 席: Senate lost too: Democratic caucus at 54
参议院更难翻，这次也翻了。民主党党团五十四席，过了五十一的半数线。: The Senate is harder to flip, and it flipped too. The Democratic caucus has fifty-four seats, past the fifty-one majority line.
全国得票领先约 13 个百分点: Leading the national vote by about 13 points
全国加起来，民主党领先十三个百分点左右。投票率接近一半，是一百多年来第二高的中期: Nationwide, Democrats lead by about thirteen points. Turnout was close to half, the second-highest midterm in more than a hundred years.
参议院：7 个州由红翻蓝: Senate: 7 states flipped red to blue
放到地图上看。带白框的七个州，原本都是共和党的参议员，这次全被翻掉。: Let's look at the map. The seven states outlined in white all had Republican senators, and every one of them flipped.
得州：38 年来第一个民主党参议员: Texas: first Democratic senator in 38 years
最让人意外的是得州。上一次得州选出民主党参议员，还是一九八八年。: The biggest surprise is Texas. The last time Texas elected a Democratic senator was nineteen eighty-eight.
缅因州，做了将近三十年参议员的柯林斯，也输了。: In Maine, Collins, a senator for nearly thirty years, lost too.
州长：5 个州由红翻蓝: Governors: 5 states flipped red to blue

州长也一样。得州、佐治亚、俄亥俄、艾奥瓦、内华达，五个州由红翻蓝。: Same with governors. Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Iowa and Nevada. Five states flipped from red to blue.
看到两院翻蓝和原因: See both chambers flip blue, and why
选民在用选票说：太贵了: Voters are saying it with their ballots: it's too expensive
为什么？最直接的答案是钱包。九成选民说生活成本是关键，三分之二认为特朗普的政策推: Why? The simplest answer is the wallet. Nine in ten voters said the cost of living was key, and two thirds think Trump's policies drove up inflation.
白宫 vs 国会：否决、停摆、调查: White House vs. Congress: vetoes, shutdowns, investigations
国会换了主人，特朗普接下来会被怎样卡住？: With Congress under new control, how will Trump be boxed in?
2027 年 1 月 3 日起：国会两院归民主党，白宫还是特朗普: From Jan. 3, 2027: Democrats hold both chambers, Trump still holds the White House
明年一月三号，新国会宣誓就职。白宫还是红的，国会变成了蓝的。这就叫分裂政府。: Next January third, the new Congress is sworn in. The White House is still red, but Congress has turned blue. That's called divided government.
两院都已通过，等待总统签字: Passed both chambers, awaiting the president's signature
法案在国会通过后，最后一步要总统签字: Once a bill passes Congress, the last step is the president's signature
民主党能在国会通过法案: Democrats can pass bills in Congress
民主党现在能让自己的法案在国会通过，然后送到白宫。: Democrats can now get their own bills through Congress and send them to the White House.
特朗普选后表态：民主党送来的“疯狂法案”，他会否决: Trump after the election: he'll veto the “crazy bills” Democrats send him
可特朗普已经放话：民主党送来的法案，他会否决。: But Trump has already said he'll veto the bills Democrats send him.
结果：谁也推不动谁，这就是僵局: Result: neither side can move the other. That's gridlock.
想推翻否决？票不够: Override the veto? Not enough votes
国会能不能推翻否决？要两院各三分之二。民主党差得很远。: Can Congress override a veto? That takes two thirds of each chamber. Democrats are nowhere close.
每一笔联邦开支都要国会批准: Every dollar of federal spending needs congressional approval
钱袋子在国会：谈不拢，政府就停摆: Congress holds the purse strings: no deal, the government shuts down
预算谈不拢，政府就停摆: No budget deal, government shuts down
更要命的是钱。政府每一笔开支都要国会批。谈不拢，政府就关门。: Even more important is money. Every dollar the government spends has to be approved by Congress. No deal, and the government shuts down.
上一次停摆：2025 年秋天，持续 43 天，史上最长: Last shutdown: fall 2025, 43 days, the longest ever
上一次停摆就在去年秋天，整整四十三天，史上最长。: The last shutdown was just last fall. Forty-three full days, the longest in history.
国会委员会要求出席听证、提交文件: Congressional committees demand testimony and documents
委员会主席换成民主党：听证、调查、传票都由他们发起: Committee chairs go to Democrats: they launch the hearings, investigations and subpoenas
还有调查。国会各委员会的主席换成民主党，听证、传票，都由他们来发。: Then there are investigations. Congressional committee chairs are now Democrats, and they decide on hearings and subpoenas.
内阁和法官提名要参议院同意：这一关也换了人: Cabinet and judicial nominees need Senate consent: that gate has new keepers too
部长和法官，要参议院点头: Secretaries and judges need the Senate's OK
最后是人事。部长、大使、联邦法官，都要参议院同意。现在这道门在民主党手里。: Finally, appointments. Cabinet secretaries, ambassadors and federal judges all need Senate approval. Now Democrats hold that gate.
先别急着说特朗普完了。一九四六年以来二十次中期选举，执政党十八次丢席，平均丢二十: Don't write Trump off just yet. In the twenty midterms since nineteen forty-six, the president's party lost seats eighteen times, twenty-six seats on average.
这一次，共和党至少丢了三十九席。比平均更惨，但还没到奥巴马二零一零年的六十三席。: This time, Republicans lost at least thirty-nine seats. Worse than average, but not as bad as Obama's sixty-three in twenty ten.
法案：国会能通过，总统能否决，谁也推不动谁: Bills: Congress can pass them, the president can veto them, neither side can budge the other
调查和人事：主动权换到民主党手里: Investigations and nominations: Democrats get the upper hand
接下来两年，大概率是僵局。法案互相卡，预算随时可能停摆，调查和人事的主动权，到了: The next two years will most likely be gridlock. Bills stall, the government could shut down at any time, and Democrats now hold the upper hand on investigations and appointments.

第一天：“分裂政府利好股市”: Day one: “divided government is good for stocks”
结果出来第一天，市场先是欢呼。道指涨了百分之三，是一年半以来最好的一天。: On the first day after the results, the market cheered. The Dow rose three percent, its best day in a year and a half.
第二天：利好只撑了一天: Day two: the boost lasted one day
可第二天，风向突变。纳斯达克跌了百分之五点五，芯片股一天跌了百分之十二，二零二零: But on day two, the mood flipped. The Nasdaq fell five and a half percent, and chip stocks dropped twelve percent in one day, their worst since March twenty twenty.
恐慌指数一天涨了七成: Fear index jumps 70% in a day
恐慌指数从十六点六一下跳到二十八。: The fear index leapt from sixteen point six to twenty-eight.
第三天：小反弹，没收复失地: Day three: small rebound, losses not recovered
周五小幅反弹，但没收复失地。: Friday brought a small rebound, but not enough to recover the losses.
云巨头涨，芯片和算力跌: Cloud giants up, chips and compute down
AI 股一半天堂一半地狱。亚马逊、微软、谷歌这些手里已经有算力的，周线反而涨；卖: For AI stocks, it was half heaven, half hell. Amazon, Microsoft and Google, the ones that already have compute, actually rose for the week. The companies selling chips and renting out compute fell across the board.
因为这是一场“数据中心选举”: Because this was a “data center election”
